ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, first and foremost is to protect the entire nation and all Indonesian territory.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded appropriately and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because such acts constitute crimes against human existence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection...
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed them in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Family...
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist medical professional who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

First Part
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government Article 7 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence in the form of:

a. establishing and ensuring the operation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements;
b. facilitating the formation of service institutions;
c. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to ensure the implementation of protection for victims by taking into account the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally.
(4) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to supervise the implementation of services for victims, with service standards that involve the community.
(5) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide funds for the protection of women and children victims of violence through the APBD as well as other sources that are legal and non-binding.
(6) The Regent appoints an Official to carry out the obligations and responsibilities of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.
